name: loft-walk-level
description: (g) LEVEL-ISOLATION-IN-WALK: walking tpl-loft's mezzanine used to hide the storey beneath it, so the overlook rendered as bare sky. Asserts walk mode renders TWO storeys where the dollhouse renders one, then stands at the mezzanine edge (via the dev-only __walkLook lever — pointer lock is unavailable headless) and shoots the overlook. With the fix disabled the same frame shows only a pale gradient beyond the rail: 57% of pixels differ, overlook-band mean luma 112.7 -> 174.4.

steps.name: dismiss-overlays
steps.eval: try { localStorage.setItem('hdb_onboarded','1') } catch {}; const s = window.__store.getState(); s.endTour?.(); s.setOnboardingOpen?.(false); s.dismissLocationPrompt?.()

steps.name: select-loft-level
steps.eval: (()=>{const s=window.__store.getState(); const up=s.floorPlan.upperLevels[0]; s.setViewLevel(up.id); return up.id})()

steps.name: walk-overlay-shown
steps.failMessage: 'Entering walkthrough' splash never appeared, so the gone-wait below would pass vacuously. If this transition genuinely raises no splash (same mode, or the room editor owns the overlay) delete BOTH guard steps rather than widening the timeout.

steps.name: walk-overlay-gone
steps.failMessage: 'Entering walkthrough' splash still up; the next screenshot would capture the splash, not the scene. See docs/visual-verification-playbook.md.

steps.name: check-two-storeys
steps.eval: (()=>{const p=window.__probe; if(!p) throw new Error('probe did not run'); if(p.visible.length!==1) throw new Error('expected 1 visible level, got '+p.visible); if(p.rendered.length!==2) throw new Error('walk mode must render the storey below too, got '+p.rendered); return p.rendered.join('+')})()

steps.name: stand-at-rail
steps.eval: (()=>{const l=window.__walkLook; if(!l||!l.setPosition) throw new Error('__walkLook.setPosition missing'); l.setPosition(2.4,3.9); l.setYaw(0); l.setPitch(-0.45); return 'at the mezzanine edge, looking over'})()
